To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the L-type calcium channel transiently expressing in HEK 93 cells inactivates during a depolarization in two phases, one that is dependent on free intracellular Ca2+, and the other that is independent on Ca2+.
the expressed L-type calcium channel is inactivated by free intracellular calcium and that the channel inactivation is voltage- and Ca2+-dependent.
the inactivation of the Ca2+ current through the L-type calcium channel is regulated by both voltage-dependent and Ca2+-dependent mechanisms.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the Ca2+- and voltage- dependent regulation of the L-type Ca(v)(1.2) calcium channel expressed in HEK293 cells.
the Ca2+-dependent inactivation of the Ca2+ channel, which plays a crucial role in the regulation of intracellular calcium concentration.
the Ca2+-dependent inactivation of the L-type channel.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the L-type Ca(v1.2) calcium channel is inactivated by Ca2+ ions with a time course that is determined by the concentration of intracellular Ca2+.

Ca2+-dependent inactivation of the L-type channel is a two-step process: (i) Ca2+-induced conformational changes of the channel protein, and (ii) a voltage-dependent transition of the channel from the open to the inactivated state.
the L-type calcium channel is a voltage-dependent, but Ca2+-sensitive, inactivated channel, and that the voltage-dependent inactivation is a minor component of the overall inactivation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the L-type calcium channel has a voltage-dependent and a Ca2+ dependent component of the inactivation.
the L-type calcium channel is inactivated in two steps.
Ca2+-dependent inactivation is a complex phenomenon involving two different mechanisms, one of them is Ca2+-dependent, the other one is voltage-dependent.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the inactivation of the L-type channel is a complex process, which is not only voltage- and Ca2+-dependent but also Na+-dependent.
the L-type calcium channel has two mechanisms of inactivation: Ca2+-dependent inactivation and voltage-dependent inactivated.
Ca2+ ions are involved in inactivation of the L-type Ca(v1.2) channel and that the Ca2+ ions can be used for modulation of the L-type current in the absence of Ca2+ influx.
